items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Mr. Beam told me that he couldn't teach me because I was colored

ctx.x: And so, I bent myself in that book every morning and every night. The people in the community were mad with me, and they called me everything but child of God. (unintelligible). Even my father got sick of me around the house. And my mother would tell my dad, 'Leave him alone. Leave him alone.'

And I sacrificed everything, all of my pleasures that a youngster would have, in order to try and learn that horn, because the man had told me that he couldn't teach me because I was colored. Mr. Beam told me that he couldn't teach me because I was colored -- after I had bought the horn from him.

I studied and studied and studied. I joined a little group, a band, a bunch of older fellows down -- who lived down from me downtown. And I used to go to rehearsals. And I'd sit up there and have the music out. I didn't know what I was doing, but I was in the band and I was trying. And they weren't much better. But we all were trying to be musicians.
